name: Sort + sliding window
space: O(1) extra (O(log n) for the sort)
whenToUse: The standard answer. Sorting costs O(n log n); the window pass after it is O(n).

card.signals: "increment by 1" means values only go up, so a group is raised to its largest value. "at most k operations" is a budget a group must stay within, and "maximum frequency" asks for the biggest group. After sorting, the best group for a target is the values just before it: a contiguous window with a rule (cost ≤ k) and a best size.
card.pattern: sort first, then a variable-size window. right picks the target value nums[right]; left moves right when the window costs too much. A running total gives the cost in O(1): cost = nums[right] × length − total.
card.coreIdea: add nums[right] to total and compute cost. While cost > k, drop nums[left], the smallest value and the most expensive to raise. Then the window length is a possible frequency: compare it with longest.

invariant: After the while loop, every value in nums[left..right] can be raised to nums[right] with at most k increments, and total is the window sum.

legend.text: left: left edge of the window
right: right edge, the target value
